study_identification_part.si4_title: Cortical thickness and grey-matter volume anomaly detection in individual MRI scans: Comparison of two methods

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its objectives: to compare anomaly detection performance of ScanOMetrics when driven by FreeSurfer vs DL+DiReCT outputs on OASIS3, and to assess suitability for clinical decision support. This satisfies both criteria: explicit research questions/hypotheses and a stated purpose of applying normative modeling in a clinical evaluation context.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Here we have compared the performance of 'ScanOMetrics' ... depending on whether it is operated on the output of FreeSurfer or ... DL+DiReCT. ... This difference in computation time might be relevant when considering application ... as diagnostic decision support"; "The purpose of this work was to explore the performance of our normative modeling approach ('ScanOMetrics') ... in the context of clinical evaluation."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: They define the reference cohort as OASIS3 healthy controls (CDR=0) and exclude "converter" subjects (those with mixed CDR=0 and CDR≥0.5 scans). They further apply image/data quality screening: LOOCV-based anomaly screening at a 5% abnormal-metrics threshold (q=0.01 per metric), IQR-based outlier removal during model fitting, and visual inspection evidence of artifacts. Final sample size is reported: 1,828 HC scans remained after removing 99 outlier HC scans from the initial 1,927 non-converting HC scans; reasons include artifacts/potential pathology and statistical outlier criteria.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Those scans were excluded from building our normative model ... based on 1'927 scans from 696 non-converting subjects"; "To clean our normative models ... remove [anomalous scans] from the normative datasets ... scans with more than 5% abnormal regions ..."; "The 99 HC scans with large number of anomalies (5.15%) were removed ... from the 1'828 remaining HC scans"; Supplement: "Outliers correspond to scans with more than 5% abnormal regions" and notes on motion/susceptibility artifacts.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age is explicitly modeled via low-order polynomials. Other covariates (sex, scanner, scanning protocol) are handled by matched subgroup selection prior to statistics, addressing multi-scanner/protocol effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "Covariates other than age (i.e. sex, scanner and scanning protocol) were accounted for by selecting matched subgroups before computing statistics." Also notes that scanner/protocol differences influence SBA estimates and require control.

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data source is clearly described as the public OASIS3 dataset, with citation, access URL, and scanner/field strength details.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The OASIS3 dataset ... is publicly available at www.oasis-brains.org ... All scans were acquired at two field strengths using Siemens MRI scanners ..."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data are used (OASIS3). Per the guide, for SECONDARY data (existing datasets) this item is not applicable.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: Uses secondary dataset OASIS3 rather than primary acquisition.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software and steps are described: FreeSurfer v6.0.0 and DL+DiReCT with default parameters; Desikan-Killiany atlas metrics exported; brain-size normalization (ICV scaling) detailed; outlier/quality control procedures outlined and applied.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "FreeSurfer ... version 6.0.0 and DL+DiReCT ... using default parameters. Results were exported in tabular form using the Desikan-Killiany atlas"; "All volumes were scaled to the mean ICV ... Mean and standard deviation of the CTh were ... scaled according to ICV^(1/3)"; "To clean our normative models ... remove [anomalous scans] ..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They use leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) on the HC reference cohort to assess internal validation, including repetition after cleaning.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "The LOOCV analysis was ... used to identify anomalous scans ... [and] repeated after cleaning of the normative dataset"; Fig. caption: "all HC scans against this subject's LOOCV model"; Supplement: "results of the LOOCV in cleaned non-converting HCs".

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study builds new normative models from OASIS3 but does not apply them to an independent external healthy dataset; analyses are confined to OASIS3.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "To achieve full reproducibility of our results, we focussed the analysis on OASIS3 ..." with no mention of external healthy validation.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: They describe the modeling: uniform age resampling, low-order polynomial fits with degree selection via nested F-tests and degree cap, outlier removal via IQR rules, uncertainty estimation from rescans, and conversion of z-scores to p-values to derive signed log10(P) anomaly scores. Software availability for ScanOMetrics is specified.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "each ... metric ... resampled ... 10-bin-histograms of the participant age ..."; "low order polynomials ... degrees ... increased ... until reduction of residual variance became insignificant (nested F tests) ... maximum degree ..."; "Before each of these fits, outliers were removed ... 1.5 inter quartile ranges ..."; "Metric variability ... measurement uncertainty derived from repeated scans ..."; "z-score ... converted to p-value ..."; "The Python3 implementation of ScanOMetrics is available at ..."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: They report quantitative calibration-like metrics for the reference cohort via LOOCV: proportion of HC scans flagged as anomalous before and after cleaning (5.15% to 1.48%) and a binomial test vs the 1% expectation at q=0.01. Although standard fit metrics (e.g., explained variance) are not reported, these quantitative indicators assess model behavior on held-out HC scans.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The 99 HC scans with large number of anomalies (5.15%) were removed ... 1'828 remaining HC scans ... [in the cleaned models] ... decreased to 27 (1.48% of HC scans, pbinom = 0.045 for fraction 1%)."

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: They use LOOCV (a partitioning strategy) rather than fixed train/validation/test splits. Overall HC sample sizes and demographics are provided (Table 1). However, characteristics for each partition/fold are not described explicitly beyond the implicit LOOCV size (n-1 training, 1 test).
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: "Demographic characteristics of the used OASIS3 subgroups" (Table 1); "LOOCV analysis ... used ... and repeated after cleaning".

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software/tools and versions are specified (FreeSurfer v6.0.0; DL+DiReCT; ScanOMetrics Python3), along with open-source code links. Supplementary materials describe saving/loading pretrained normative model files (e.g., Polynomial_dldirect_cleanOASIS3), indicating availability and versioning of models.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "The Python3 implementation of ScanOMetrics is available at ..."; "FreeSurfer ... version 6.0.0 and DL+DiReCT ..."; Supplement: "ScanOMetrics is distributed with a selection of pre-trained normative models ... 'Polynomial_dldirect_cleanOASIS3' and 'Polynomial_freesurfer_cleanOASIS3'".

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical cohort is from the secondary OASIS3 dataset. Eligibility is described via CDR-based categorization (patients with established AD: CDR≥1), and final sample size is reported. However, explicit image quality/data completeness standards for the clinical cohort are not detailed beyond general discussion of artifacts.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "The OASIS3 dataset ... contains ... patients with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and healthy controls (HC)"; "The AD dataset consisted of 209 scans with CDR ≥ 1.0"; Discussion of motion artifacts in rescans (example), but no explicit clinical-cohort QC criteria.

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: They analyze deviation patterns stratified by clinical dementia rating (CDR) levels (0.5, 1, ≥2), a clinical severity measure. Other clinical covariates (e.g., medication, illness duration) are not modeled.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "Percentage of CTh anomalies ... stratified by cognitive impairment levels at scan time (CDR = 0.5 ... CDR = 1 ... CDR ≥ 2)"; "an apparent worsening of atrophy ... revealed ... by the CTh anomaly maps, see Fig. 2".

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical cohort data source is specified as OASIS3 with citation and scanning details.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "The OASIS3 dataset ... is publicly available ... contains ... scans ... field strengths and scanner types ..."

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: They report clinical cohort sample sizes and demographics (age and sex) in Table 1 for CDR≥1. Clinical characteristics beyond CDR (e.g., medication status) are not detailed.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: Table 1 provides participants, scans, and age (mean±SD, range) for CDR ≥ 1; female counts are also given.

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: CDR is specified and used to stratify analyses. The assessment procedure details are not described here (standard for OASIS3).
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "clinical dementia rating (CDR)" referenced multiple times; stratification by CDR levels in Fig. 2.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: They define deviation scores as signed log10(P): positive for larger-than-expected values and negative for smaller-than-expected, with a quantitative abnormality threshold (q=0.01). They interpret clinical significance by linking deviation patterns to known AD atrophy regions and stratifying by CDR, and discuss implications (e.g., entorhinal thinning, hippocampal volume reductions).
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "log10(P), signed positive/negative for larger/smaller than expected fit residues, were used as the central objects ... To detect a statistical anomaly, a significance threshold was set to q = 0.01"; "the bilateral entorhinal gyrus was identified as one of the earliest visible and most prominent deviations in patients with AD ..."; "Progression of the atrophy pattern with clinical dementia rating (CDR) was clearly observable".
